title: Mini-Project: Cross-AI Review Orchestrator
objective: Apply workspace and collaboration concepts to extend skeptic with a cross-AI review orchestrator that dispatches reviews to multiple AI runtimes, aggregates results, and formats combined output

content.value:
Look at the skeptic command you have built across six modules. In Module 1 you wrote the command spec. In Module 2 you added the handler. In Module 3 you made findings persist. In Module 4 you added orchestration with parallel review subagents. In Module 5 you added quality verification that checks the review's own output. In Module 6 you added a dispatch loop that reads state, routes focused reviews, and tracks coverage.

But every review dispatched by your skeptic goes to a single AI runtime -- Claude. Compare that to GSD's /gsd:review command from Lesson 3: it dispatches the same review prompt to multiple AI runtimes (Claude, Cursor, Gemini) and combines their perspectives. Different runtimes catch different things. One spots architectural issues, another catches convention violations, a third finds edge cases.

Module 7 closes this gap. You will add a cross-AI review orchestrator to your skeptic workflow -- a mechanism that dispatches review requests to multiple AI runtimes (not just Claude), collects their findings, aggregates results with attribution, and formats a unified review report. This is the cross-AI peer review pattern applied to your skeptic.
content.focus: The skeptic journey across 7 modules -- Module 1 command spec, Module 2 handler, Module 3 persistence, Module 4 orchestration, Module 5 quality verification, Module 6 dispatch loop. Now adding cross-AI review dispatch.

content.value:
Below is a workflow template that adds a cross-AI review orchestrator to your existing skeptic workflow. Press C to copy, then integrate it into your workflow at ~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/skeptic.md. The key addition is a cross-AI review step that dispatches review requests to multiple AI runtimes (not just Claude), collects their findings, and merges them into unified output. Place this after or within the dispatch loop from Module 6.

The specific runtimes, invocation methods, deduplication strategy, and report format are yours to customize.
content.focus: Introducing the cross-AI review orchestrator template

content.value:
<!-- Cross-AI review orchestrator (inspired by /gsd:review multi-runtime pattern) -->

<step name="cross_ai_review">
**Dispatch reviews to multiple AI runtimes and aggregate their findings.**

## Runtime Registry
List of AI runtimes to dispatch reviews to:
- claude: Primary review runtime
- cursor: Secondary review runtime
- gemini: Tertiary review runtime
(Add or remove runtimes based on availability)

## Dispatch to Runtimes
For each runtime in the registry:
1. Format a review prompt with the scoped context from the dispatch loop
2. Invoke the runtime with the formatted prompt
3. Collect the runtime's response and findings

## Result Aggregation
Merge findings from all runtimes:
- Deduplicate overlapping findings from different runtimes
- Note which runtime produced each finding (attribution)
- Reconcile conflicting assessments across runtimes

## Output Formatting
Produce a unified review report:
- Per-runtime sections showing each runtime's individual findings
- Combined findings summary with deduplicated results
- Attribution markers indicating the source runtime for each finding
</step>
content.focus: Cross-AI review step with runtime registry, multi-runtime dispatch, result aggregation with deduplication and attribution, and formatted output

content.value:
Make it yours. The six structural requirements that verification checks for are:

1. Runtime registry -- defines or lists multiple AI runtimes to dispatch to
2. Multi-runtime dispatch -- sends review requests to more than one runtime
3. Result collection -- collects or receives responses from dispatched runtimes
4. Result aggregation -- merges or combines findings from multiple sources
5. Runtime attribution -- tracks which runtime produced which finding
6. Output formatting -- produces formatted combined review output

Everything else -- the specific runtimes you list, how you invoke them, your deduplication strategy, the report format, whether you add runtime-specific review prompts or use the same prompt for all -- is your creative decision. Verification checks structure, not content.
content.focus: Six structural requirements with creative freedom for everything else

In Module 1 you wrote a command spec -- a blueprint. In Module 2 you built the handler that executes it. In Module 3 you added persistence so findings accumulate. Your skeptic started as a single command spec. Now it is a multi-runtime review orchestrator with persistence, parallel execution, quality verification, autonomous dispatch, and cross-AI collaboration. Seven modules. Seven layers. Each one built on the last. Module 7 complete.
